nodes.label: drills/*.json
nodes.summary: The drill library — one human-readable JSON file per drill. This folder IS the database and the agent interface.
nodes.details: Filename = drill id. Agents (Claude Code / Codex) write here directly; the app reads and writes through the server. Sparse steps are legal on disk; the app saves dense. Git history doubles as backup.

nodes.label: data/ (rosters, settings, trash)
nodes.summary: Per-machine personal data: the team roster (kids' names — gitignored), app settings, and the soft-delete trash.
nodes.details: Deletes never destroy: drills move to data/trash/ with a timestamp and can be restored from the library's trash dialog. Rosters and settings are gitignored so children's names never reach the public repo.

nodes.label: exports/<drill>/
nodes.summary: Generated media: PNG, MP4/WebM, GIF, narrated takes, and the site-bundle/ folder handed to the team-site agent.
nodes.details: Gitignored output. site-bundle/ contains poster PNG + GIF + MP4 + drill JSON + manifest-snippet.json (matching the soccer-quizzes site's manifest shape) + AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS.md telling the site agent where each file goes.

nodes.label: Agent docs & schema
nodes.summary: drill-authoring.md (canonical format guide), CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and the generated JSON Schema — how AIs learn to write drills.
nodes.details: npm run validate checks structure (zod) + semantics (anchor refs, step windows, id/filename match). npm run schema regenerates schema/drill.schema.json from the zod source so editors and agents validate while typing.

nodes.label: Express file API
nodes.summary: Dumb CRUD on 127.0.0.1:8123: drills, rosters, settings, trash, export blobs, site bundles. No business logic.
nodes.details: Atomic writes (tmp + rename), rev stamping with If-Match conflict checks (409), delete-to-trash, slug validation guarding Windows reserved filenames, port probing 8123-8130. Serves dist/ as the SPA and this atlas at /atlas.

nodes.label: chokidar → SSE
nodes.summary: Watches drills/ and pushes drills-changed events so agent-written files appear in the library within ~1s.
nodes.details: awaitWriteFinish debounces partial writes; /api/events is a plain EventSource stream with heartbeats. This is what makes the agent route feel live.

nodes.label: API client
nodes.summary: Typed fetch wrappers for every server route plus the SSE subscription.
nodes.details: Thin and dependency-free; ApiError carries status + body so persistence can branch on 409 conflicts.

nodes.label: Persistence orchestrator
nodes.summary: Autosave (debounced, drag-aware), SSE-driven reloads, own-write echo suppression, and the conflict ladder.
nodes.details: Tracks the drill object reference that matches disk (savedRef) to tell edits from loads. On SSE for the open drill: same rev = own write (ignore); not dirty = silent reload; dirty = conflict modal (keep mine = force PUT, use disk = reload). Also boot, open/new/duplicate/delete flows.

nodes.label: Data model (types + zod)
nodes.summary: The drill format: entities, sparse keyframe steps, annotations with anchors and visibility windows. Meters everywhere.
nodes.details: types.ts is the TS source of truth; schema.ts is its zod mirror (a compile-time check stops drift). parseDrill is forgiving: unknown position keys are dropped, sparse steps are legal.

nodes.label: Timeline & resolver
nodes.summary: Compiles steps into hold/move/pause segments and produces the board for any instant: sceneAt(t) tweens poses and fades notation.
nodes.details: Sparse forward-fill (pose at step k = last explicit pose at or before k), Catmull-Rom via-waypoints, shortest-arc rotation, instant ease, anchored arrow endpoints re-resolved every frame so they track runners, 150ms fades for step-scoped annotations.

nodes.label: Dense serializer
nodes.summary: Wire/file form: forward-fill materialized, coords rounded to cm, via/ease only where explicit, undefined keys dropped.
nodes.details: The app saves dense so every step reads independently; agents may write sparse and the next app save normalizes.

nodes.label: Formation presets
nodes.summary: One-click team placement: preset shapes per format, slot labels, roster matching (position-exact first, then in order).
nodes.details: Roster jersey numbers win; default numbers skip them so a team never shows duplicate shirts.

nodes.label: zustand store + zundo
nodes.summary: All editor state and actions. Only `drill` is history-tracked; a whole drag coalesces into one undo entry.
nodes.details: Playback (mode/time/speed/loop), selection, tools, step operations with annotation index remapping, dialogs, toasts. The gesture trick: pause history on drag start, rewind to the stashed base, replay the final state as one tracked change.

nodes.label: PitchSpec table
nodes.summary: Data-driven pitch geometry: 11v11, 9v9, 8v8, half-pitch, training grid — one renderer reads the spec.
nodes.details: Lengths/widths in meters, end markings mirrored from one definition, per-format token scale so pieces stay legible, 3m apron of legal off-pitch space.

nodes.label: BoardSvg — THE renderer
nodes.summary: Pure snapshot → SVG. The live editor and every export draw through this one component.
nodes.details: Constraint that keeps exports working: no foreignObject, no webfonts, no external hrefs. Editor-only chrome (selection handles, draw previews) comes in as children so the renderer itself stays export-safe.

nodes.label: Tokens & notation glyphs
nodes.summary: Players, ball, seven equipment kinds, and coaching arrows (pass/run/dribble/shot), zones, labels.
nodes.details: Arrows use explicit head polygons (not SVG markers) and dark underlays for contrast — both choices keep SVG-to-canvas rasterization faithful.

nodes.label: Interaction & viewport
nodes.summary: Pointer state machine (drag, draw arrows/zones, re-anchor endpoints, resize) plus CSS-transform zoom/pan.
nodes.details: Arrow ends snap to players/ball and follow them. getScreenCTM() folds the zoom transform into pointer math, so zooming changed nothing in the interaction code.

nodes.label: Timeline & transport
nodes.summary: Edit/Preview modes, play/scrub/loop/speed, the step strip (jump, reorder, duplicate, delete, inline durations).
nodes.details: The clock advances by real elapsed time via rAF plus a watchdog interval, so hidden tabs never freeze playback.

nodes.label: Library, inspector, dialogs
nodes.summary: Searchable library with live mini-board previews, context-sensitive inspector, roster/place-team/settings/trash/record dialogs.
nodes.details: Library previews render the actual drill JSON through a mini BoardSvg — nothing to go stale. The inspector edits whatever is selected: player identity, arrow style + visibility window, zone caption, step timing.

nodes.label: renderFrames generator
nodes.summary: The offline frame loop: sceneAt(t) → BoardSvg markup → rasterize to one reused canvas at a fixed timestep.
nodes.details: Deterministic (no realtime capture, no dropped frames), abortable, even-numbered dimensions for H.264. Every visual export consumes this generator.

nodes.label: MP4 / WebM / GIF / PNG
nodes.summary: WebCodecs + mediabunny encode H.264 MP4 (VP9/WebM fallback); gifenc quantizes per-frame palettes; PNG snapshots any instant.
nodes.details: runExport guards one job at a time with progress modal + cancel (AbortSignal threads through the frame loop). The site bundle orchestrates PNG + GIF + MP4 then asks the server to assemble site-bundle/.

nodes.label: Narrated takes
nodes.summary: Region-Capture tab recording cropped to the board + mic, MediaRecorder MP4/WebM — the one live (non-rasterized) capture.
nodes.details: Mic check with level meter, 3-2-1 countdown, floating stop bar, red board ring; the browser's own Stop-sharing pill ends the take cleanly; 1s timeslices bound data loss.

edges.label: agents write drills following the guide
